pattern_id: Crash-induced SafetyRules regression with double voting and conflicting QCs
description: In Aptos HotStuff, each validator runs SafetyRules in a separate process with locally persisted SafetyData (last_voted_round, preferred_round/lock, last_vote, etc.). If persistence/recovery is not crash-atomic, an honest validator can sign a vote in round r for block A, then crash before the updated SafetyData is durably persisted. On restart, SafetyRules is reconstructed from stale SafetyData that only reflects an older state (e.g., last_voted_round = r-1, last_vote = Vote(A1) or None). A byzantine leader can then drive a conflicting branch and request a second vote in round r (or a higher round) for a conflicting block B. Because SafetyRules trusts the regressed state, it may accept and sign Vote(B, r) even though it previously signed Vote(A, r). Embedding these votes into an n = 3f+1 = 4 validator set with at most f = 1 byzantine validator allows the construction of two conflicting QCs for A and B at the same epoch/round whose voter sets intersect in an honest validator, enabling double-commit scenarios.
trigger_condition: 1) Honest validator V signs a vote for block A at (epoch, round r), updating in-memory SafetyData but not yet persisting it. 2) V crashes and restarts from stale SafetyData that records only voting up to round < r on branch A (or records no last_vote at all). 3) After restart, a byzantine leader proposes a conflicting block B in the same (epoch, round r) or at a higher round extending a conflicting chain. 4) SafetyRules reconstructs its state solely from stale SafetyData and accepts a second vote for B, yielding two signed votes by V that are not ancestor/descendant-related.
test_template: At the SafetyRules level: (1) Use a single-validator epoch to obtain an EpochState and genesis QC. (2) Manually construct SafetyData pre-state S_pre with some last_voted_round r0 and initialize SafetyRules with S_pre. (3) Build a branch A: propose A1 at round r1 and A2 at round r2; call construct_and_sign_vote_two_chain to obtain votes for A1 and A2, and record the resulting SafetyData S_true from persistent_storage. (4) Emulate a crash by dropping SafetyRules and reinitializing it with a stale SafetyData S_stale that only records voting up to round r1 (or r0) and, optionally, last_vote = Vote(A1) or None. (5) Build a conflicting branch B (e.g., B1 at r1, B2 at r2) that is not on the same chain as A2. (6) Call construct_and_sign_vote_two_chain on B2 using the restarted SafetyRules. If this succeeds and the proposed id differs from A2, embed vote(A2) and vote(B2) into a synthetic n = 4 validator set {V0 (byzantine), V1, V2 (crashable honest), V3} and construct two QCs: QC_A2 with voters {V0,V1,V2} and QC_B2 with voters {V0,V2,V3}. Assert both QCs verify, certify different blocks, have size 2f+1, and that their voter sets intersect in the honest V2. The test should fail (panic) when such conflicting QCs are constructible, indicating a SafetyRules crash-recovery bug.
